shared_elements: monolithic upright stone block with a broad, flatter top section
shallow low-relief carving on a curved/flat stone face
horizontal band of repeated linear pattern (zigzag/incised strokes vs. incised belt lines)
division of the surface into stacked horizontal registers
justification: Both are tall monolithic stones photographed from below, whose carved faces are organised into stacked horizontal registers, with a broad top block above a transverse patterned band and disc/arc motifs beneath — the register-plus-band scheme is the most specific correspondence. The decisive difference is content and handling: B carries crisp figurative animals and arm-like limbs in confident low relief, while A is almost wholly abstract, worn and reduced to rings, arcs and belt lines with no living creatures.
